points: Q3 2026 will show whether the 12% organic ARR growth and 38% SaaS mix from Q2 carried into the summer, since that recurring-revenue base underpins the 18.8% FY1 EPS growth consensus is pricing in.

FinTech momentum is the key engine to watch: Q2 FinTech revenue rose 15% organic and FinTech ARR grew 16% organic, with 58 new clients and cross-sells above 15% of the pipeline, so Q3 new-business metrics will signal whether Q4 stays on track.

Index revenue and ETP flows are a critical read: Q2 index revenue jumped 35% adjusted on $51 billion of net inflows, and Q3 flow data will reveal if the $1 trillion AUM milestone is still expanding and supporting Capital Access Platforms.

Expense discipline sets up the following quarters: management guided 2026 non-GAAP operating expenses to $2.530 billion-$2.570 billion and a 22.5%-24.5% tax rate, and any Q3 update will shape the 13.1% year-two EPS growth consensus expects.

Reports suggest Nasdaq raised its medium-term revenue outlook at its 2026 Investor Day, so the Q3 call may add detail on how that outlook feeds into Q4 and 2027, particularly around AI-driven market modernization and new listings.

The fintech theme is active and leaning long, and the 16/0 upward analyst revision skew over the past 30 days aligns with the long side; the SEZL peer print on Nov. 6 could provide a cross-read on fintech demand.

Valuation is flagged as fair at roughly 1.0x the theme median on P/E and PEG, so the trade rests on execution rather than multiple expansion; Q3 needs to confirm the ~24x forward P/E is backed by durable double-digit Solutions and ARR growth.
watch: ARR organic growth holds at or above 12% — supports the long
Solutions revenue growth stays at or above 17% — supports the long
FinTech ARR growth stays around 16% with continued new-client/cross-sell flow — supports the long
2026 non-GAAP operating expenses remain within the $2.530B-$2.570B guided range — supports the long
